review_notes: I reviewed the whole file, which has one theorem and one simp call. I read `pathLaw_def` and `pathLaw_coord` in PathLaw/Basic.lean and searched for uses of `pathLaw_def` across TauCeti. I did not run Lean. I did not check how `pathLaw_coord` would interact with `pathLaw_def` as simp rules, nor what a priority annotation would do to other `simp` calls that rely on `pathLaw_def`. That is why the proposal is hedged.

findings.excerpt: have hpath : pathLaw ρ (fun n (x : ℕ → α) => x n) = ρ := by simp [pathLaw_def]
findings.problem: The coordinate-process normal form `pathLaw ρ (fun n x => x n) = ρ` has a named lemma, `pathLaw_coord`, but it is not a simp lemma. The proof therefore passes `pathLaw_def` to simp, which unfolds `pathLaw` to `Measure.map (fun ω i => ...)`. Simp then has to recognise the result as `Measure.map id`. The same `simp [pathLaw_def]` workaround appears in ZeroOne.lean line 68, where the same `hpath` fact is rebuilt. `pathLaw_def` is itself `@[simp]`, so the named `pathLaw` is unfolded everywhere and the interface lemma never gets a chance to fire.
findings.proposed_change: Here, replace the `by simp [pathLaw_def]` proof with `pathLaw_coord ρ`, which is the existing lemma. More generally, mark `pathLaw_coord` `@[simp]` and give it higher priority than `pathLaw_def`, so the canonical rewrite `pathLaw ρ coord = ρ` wins over the unfolding. Alternatively, drop `@[simp]` from `pathLaw_def` and keep it as an explicit rewrite lemma. Then drop the `simp [pathLaw_def]` workarounds here and in ZeroOne.lean.
findings.benefit: Simp goals with `pathLaw ρ (fun n x => x n)` normalise directly to `ρ` instead of through an unfolded `map`. The `hpath` boilerplate in this file and in ZeroOne.lean shrinks, and the proofs no longer depend on the internal definition of `pathLaw`.

evidence.excerpt: theorem pathLaw_coord (ρ : Measure (ℕ → α)) : pathLaw ρ (fun i (x : ℕ → α) => x i) = ρ := by
theorem pathLaw_def (μ : Measure Ω) (X : ℕ → Ω → α) :
have hpath : pathLaw ρ (fun n (x : ℕ → α) => x n) = ρ := by simp [pathLaw_def]
